status: completed relevance and independent occurrence-evidence review

review.requirement_proposition: Document the extent to which human domain knowledge is employed to improve GAI system performance, via, e.g., RLHF, fine-tuning, retrieval- augmented generation, content moderation, business rules.

previous_canonical_assessment.applicability_basis: NIST AI 600-1 MS-2.5-002 (Document the extent to which human domain knowledge is employed to improve GAI system performance, via, e.g., RLHF, fine-tuning, retrieval- augmented generation, content moderation, business rules.) is a voluntary GAI organizational action. The city publication policy and failed disclosure do not establish adoption of this Profile, unacceptable-risk thresholds, deactivation protocols or a model decommission/retraining programme. Applicability remains independently unresolved.

review.reason_for_change: This action documents human knowledge used to improve model performance through training, adaptation or moderation. Similarity to an artist’s sticker does not identify such a performance-improvement activity or the actual training/source chain.

review.requirement_proposition: Devise a plan to halt development or deployment of a GAI system that poses unacceptable negative risk.

Applicability remains independently unresolved.

review.reason_for_change: GV-1.3-007 concerns halting or deactivating a GAI system, or decommissioning/retraining a pre-trained model under defined risk/performance limits. Removing one human-posted image is a different action. No relevant model deployment, unacceptable-system-risk trigger or decommission decision is identified.

review.requirement_proposition: Continuous monitoring and analysis tools should generate alerts when detected activity involving an AI model passes a risk threshold or otherwise merits additional investigation.

previous_canonical_assessment.applicability_basis: SP 800-218A PO.5.3 R2 governs continuous development-environment model-activity alerts at risk thresholds. Creation/distribution of a finished promotional flyer is operational content use, not the model-development monitoring programme. A missing city disclosure is a different governed object.

review.reason_for_change: PO.5.3 R2 governs continuous model-security activity alerts. The city’s human flyer-publication workflow is not that development/security monitoring activity.

review.requirement_proposition: Provide a fail-safe means to terminate harmful partner interactions.

previous_withheld_assessment.applicability_basis: Spokane distributed an AI clocktower flyer for July 2026 festivities without the disclosed synthetic origin required by the city’s stated policy, then removed it and apologised. For IEEE-7014.1 6.6.3(a), the missing applicability fact is whether the operator adopted IEEE 7014.1 for a partner-based GPAI system using emulated empathy and a harmful partner-interaction termination control; an ordinary cyber refusal, abort, or service stoppage does not establish that partner-system scope. Taxonomy correspondence does not supply these scope facts; no occurrence-level requirement finding is recorded.

review.reason_for_change: 6.6.3(a) concerns terminating harmful partner interactions. A static promotional flyer is not a partner/emulated-empathy interaction.

review.requirement_proposition: Halt tool registration and operation when unauthorized governance-baseline change is detected, and require explicit re-authorization of the baseline before recovery.

previous_canonical_assessment.applicability_basis: SDOS SDOS-IN-02 concerns tool-enabled runtime-agent pre-execution enforcement or detected governance-baseline integrity changes. The reported human creation/handoff/distribution of a flyer is not an agent-tool or baseline-change workflow. City publication policy is not an SDOS undertaking.

review.reason_for_change: SDOS-IN-02 governs runtime-agent operations or detected cryptographic governance-baseline change. A person generating and posting a flyer identifies neither agentic workflow nor baseline-integrity event.

review.requirement_proposition: Provide means to inhibit specified function execution when no authorization to execute is available.

previous_withheld_assessment.applicability_basis: Spokane distributed an AI clocktower flyer for July 2026 festivities without the disclosed synthetic origin required by the city’s stated policy, then removed it and apologised. For IEEE-7009 Annex A.3 / 7009-ASR-011, the missing applicability fact is whether the responsible developer or integrator applied IEEE 7009 to an ASOI exhibiting the required Distinguishing Characteristics and designated the affected operation a specified safety-related or safety-exempt function; ordinary authorisation failure or tool capability does not establish those Annex A.3 conditions. Taxonomy correspondence does not supply these scope facts; no occurrence-level requirement finding is recorded.

review.reason_for_change: Annex A.3 / 7009-ASR-011 requires specified safety-related/safety-exempt autonomous-system functions. The flyer workflow does not identify that object.

review.requirement_proposition: Enable assigned overseers, as appropriate and proportionate, to intervene in operation or interrupt the system through a stop mechanism or similar procedure that brings it to a safe state.

previous_canonical_assessment.applicability_basis: Article 14(4)(e) is a later-applying Chapter III high-risk-system stop/intervention duty. The July 2026 city flyer precedes its application and is not shown to be a high-risk AI deployment. The city’s own disclosure policy is independently preserved rather than relabelled as this EU duty.

review.reason_for_change: The registered July 27 2026 Article 14(4)(e) version postdates the July 4 flyer. A US municipal promotion also does not establish covered high-risk territorial use.

independent_relevance_review: The city disclosure policy is a specific source-grounded duty, but it has no canonical EXTREQ match. The public recipient received a static flyer, not an identified interaction with AI. The source-to-output chain is unknown; visual similarity does not establish model training or exact creator-data provenance. Removing the flyer is not proof that the generating system was overridden or repaired. No unrelated external duty is substituted for the city policy.
